text:
maya: heads up — noticed a couple internal requests failing telemetry because X-Subaccount is being stripped at the gateway. looks like the global header-scrub rule removed it.
aj: ouch. which rule? the aggressive privacy scrub we rolled out? :grimacing:
maya: i think so. the rule currently strips any header matching /^X-Internal-|^X-Private-/ and also removes unknown x- headers. that caught X-Subaccount (we prefix it with X-).
sam: that will break quota attribution and per-tenant routing if the header disappears. we need an allowlist for headers used by routing and billing.
cheng: agreed. should we make routing headers opt-in via route config? e.g. route.policy.rewrite.allow_headers = ["X-Subaccount","X-Client-ID"]
aj: i'd prefer default deny but a global exception list for critical internal headers. less footguns for teams.
helena: can we instead canonicalize these into a single header like X-Redwood-Tenant and drop all others? that helps normalization for downstream services.
maya: that would require us to map incoming variants (x-subaccount, x-sub-account, x-redwood-tenant). we already run header-normalization, but order matters. currently header-scrub runs after normalization -> it deletes the canonicalized header.
sam: oh nice catch. so the sequence is: 1) path normalization 2) header canonicalization 3) header-scrub. if scrub runs last, it wipes things.
cheng: solution options: move scrub earlier, make scrub aware of canonical names, or change scrub to 'strip-except' with an allowlist per route.
aj: moving scrub earlier could leak raw headers to auth hooks (bad). prefer scrub-aware canonicalization or per-route allowlist.
maya: quick prototyping suggestion — add a route-level block: 
```
route: "/v1/*"
rewrite: {
  headers: {
    remove: ["X-Debug-Token"],
    map: {"x-subaccount":"X-Redwood-Tenant"},
    allowlist: ["X-Redwood-Tenant","X-Client-Region"]
  },
  query: {
    remove: ["debug","profile"]
  },
  path: {normalize_trailing_slash: true, lowercase: true}
}
```
aj: looks reasonable. note: query param removal must happen before signature validation. otherwise existing signed URLs will fail.
helena: good call. also need to preserve original path in X-Forwarded-Path for debugging (but redacted in logs).
sam: can we add a safe-mode for rollout: a flag to do dry-run rewrites and telemetry diffs? e.g. rewrite.dry_run=true -> no actual mutate, emit what would change.
maya: yes, we have the telemetry hooks — we can add a metric that counts "would_have_removed_header:X-Subaccount". that will help test.
cheng: about path normalization: lowercase vs case-sensitive services — some customers still rely on case. we should make lowercase optional per route and default to false for backwards compat.
aj: agreed default false. enable for routes with downstream services that are known-safe.
helena: also note when we remove query params like debug, we should preserve them in an unobtrusive header for internal debugging: X-Orig-Query="debug=1&profile=1" (base64 encode if necessary).
sam: don't forget caching implications. removing query params can change cache keys. need to update the cache-keying policy when we rewrite queries.
maya: I'll open a tiny RFC + prototype branch: implement per-route allowlist, dry-run telemetry, and query-removal-with-x-orig. will add tests for ordering vs sig check.
aj: thanks. can you throw a short test matrix in the RFC: cases for signed-url, cache, tenant header present/missing, trailing slash variants.
maya: yep. i'll paste matrix when I open the PR.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: gateway-rewrite-proto -> staging at 2026-03-05T18:00Z (ci:green).
helena: perfect — let's gate on dry-run metrics for 48h before enabling mutating rewrites. :thumbsup:
maya: ack. starting RFC now.
aj: ping me on the PR for review, will look at security implications.
cheng: i'll add unit tests for header mapping and ensure scrub doesn't run after the final canonicalization step in staging.
sam: thanks team — this should stop the tenant attribution regressions.
maya: thanks all!
